text:
anya: Quick post-sync note: proposing a lightweight \"soft-grace\" evaluator that prefers local mitigations then short-lived borrow from a global pool before any hard denials. Thoughts?

mike: +1. Keep evaluator decisions minimal (ok / borrow(N) / degrade(list) / deny). Runtime picks variant.

sophia: What about abuse? Tenants could hammer borrow.

linh: Add sliding-window counters + decaying borrow score. Borrow allowed only if borrowed_in_window < limit && tenant_abuse_score < threshold.

raj: Where does the pool live? Central allocator with hot local caches sounds right. Need idempotent receipts to prevent double counting.

mike: Agreed. Borrow TTL short (10-30s) and small amounts. Also per-tenant cap + per-route subcap.

ops-bot: deploy-check: add policy/soft-grace dry_run flag -> /deploys/policy-soft-grace-dryrun

sophia: Observability: emit fallback.reason tag, borrow_tokens, borrow_latency, and traces that mark fallback.step. Dry-run should log "would_*" decisions.

linh: Interface boundary: evaluator returns compact tuple only. Keep headers small: X-Redwood-Fallback-Code and X-Redwood-Borrow-Tokens. SDK surfaces fallback_code.

anya: Rollout plan: dry-run -> canary tenants -> alpha -> global. Acceptance: no 99p regression on high-priority routes.

mike: I'll draft RFC: config schema, prom queries, test plan. Raj coordinate tenants and tests.

ops-bot: synthetic-burst test scheduled 2024-09-20T03:00Z
